html:
The Quiet Revolution was a time of rapid change in Quebec in the 1960s under the Liberal government of Jean Lesage, elected in 1960. It ended the long rule of Maurice Duplessis and the power of the Catholic Church over schools and welfare.

The province created a ministry of education, built a welfare state and nationalised the private power companies into Hydro-Quebec, a project led by Rene Levesque. The slogan was "masters in our own house".

French speaking Quebecers gained confidence and economic power. Some wanted independence: Levesque founded the Parti Quebecois in 1968, and a radical fringe turned to bombs, leading to the October Crisis. Quebecers voted no to sovereignty in 1980 and again, by a hair, in 1995. Pierre Trudeau answered with bilingualism and the Charter.
